item.title: Stiftung Künstler*dorf Schöppingen: Residency Fellowship 2027 Open Call
item.description:
Organisation: Stiftung Künstler*dorf Schöppingen

Location: Schöppingen, Germany (residency requires living and working on-site)

Award: Stipend of EUR 1,500 per month, minus roughly EUR 100-200 for rent and operating expenses. For collectives, EUR 1,000 per person up to a maximum of EUR 3,000 per month, minus rent and operating costs. Travel, insurance and material costs are covered only in exceptional cases, on request.

Duration: Residency of two to six months during 2027; period chosen by agreement and availability

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Stiftung Künstler*dorf Schöppingen offers residency fellowships for professional visual artists, authors and composers; since 2023 applications from collectives are also accepted. The call is open to people of all nationalities and ages, and accommodation for partners, family members or assistance can be arranged upon agreement and availability (for physical, cognitive or sensory disabilities, contact the foundation to explain any barriers). Fellows reside and work at the Künstler*dorf for a period of their choosing between two and six months, using the premises and infrastructure on-site. The stipend is EUR 1,500 per month, minus roughly EUR 100-200 for rent and operating expenses; for collectives it is EUR 1,000 per person up to a maximum of EUR 3,000 per month, minus rent and operating costs. Travel, insurance or material costs are covered only in exceptional cases on request. The fellowship is not designed as a production residency and there is no obligation to present results, though exhibition and presentation facilities are available and the voluntary co-organization of events (lectures, readings, workshops or similar) is welcomed. A willingness to participate in events and to engage in exchange with other fellows is a prerequisite. Selection is made by expert juries on the quality of previous work, the quality and plausibility of the project for Schöppingen, and program contributions (interaction / community building). Applications for 2027 can be submitted from 27 June to 31 August 2026 (midnight CET) via the online application portal.

item.title: Accent Sisters Work-Study Fellowship Program 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Accent Sisters

Location: 89 5th Ave, Suite 702, New York, NY 10003 (hybrid; part-time, 3 days/week, on-site work required)

Award: Stipend of USD 600 (paid in two installments), plus free passes to all in-person events and classes, fellow discounts, and one-on-one mentorship.

Duration: 20 August to 20 December 2026; part-time, 3 days per week

Deadline: 01 Aug 2026

Accent Sisters offers a work-study fellowship for individuals passionate about literature, visual arts, and community engagement. The fellowship provides hands-on experience in a bookstore and a hybrid event space where exhibitions, book launches, film screenings, educational programs, and other public programming take place. It is ideal for someone looking to build a career in cultural institutions, independent bookstores, or art galleries. Fellows work closely with both the bookstore and gallery teams, gaining skills in book curation, exhibit planning, marketing, and community outreach, while developing a personal project that merges these disciplines. WHAT YOU GET: opportunities to work with writers, artists, and creators; a chance to pitch projects, events, and programs for a diverse community; free passes to all in-person events and classes; fellow discounts; a showcase of your personal project toward the end of the fellowship; one-on-one mentorship with the Accent team; and a USD 600 stipend. Open to upcoming seniors, upcoming second-year graduate students, and recent graduates of undergraduate/graduate programs. Four tracks are offered and applicants generally choose one: Program Coordination & Community Engagement; Curation & Administration; Graphic Design & Digital Asset Management; or Marketing & Business Development. The fellowship runs 20 August to 20 December 2026 (part-time, 3 days per week, on-site required). Applications are reviewed from 15 July to 1 August 2026.

item.title: The Gallery at Penn College: 2027-28 Call for Exhibitions
item.description:
Organisation: The Gallery at Penn College (Pennsylvania College of Technology)

Location: Williamsport, Pennsylvania, USA, on the Pennsylvania College of Technology campus. Travel note: Williamsport Regional Airport connects only to Washington Dulles, with no other direct flights or trains, so international travel involves a connection. No nationality restriction is stated.

Award: Housing, meals, a solo exhibition honorarium, and a shipping and travel stipend are all provided. Specific figures are not published in the call. No application fee is stated.

Duration: Exhibition slot within the 2027-28 season; review takes place during autumn semester with artists notified in January

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Gallery at Penn College is accepting proposals for solo, two-person and group exhibitions in its 2027-28 season. All entries are juried through a blind selection process by a gallery committee of faculty, staff, K-12 art educators and community artists. The space is 3,000 square feet with 82 to 250 running feet of linear wall depending on configuration and a ceiling height of 11 feet 4 inches, and all exhibitions are installed by gallery staff. Site-specific installations requiring artist installation need an approved planning document first. Campus visits are a valued part of programming though some exhibitions are scheduled without one; visiting artists give a 20 to 30 minute gallery talk at the public reception, and are encouraged to propose class-specific programmes or community workshops. Promotional support includes an annual gallery catalogue, postcards, press releases and web and social coverage. Applications require 10 to 15 digital images (JPG only, max 4 MB each), an image list with dimensions and medium, a CV and an artist statement.

item.title: Kulturstiftung des Bundes: General Project Funding (Allgemeine Projektfoerderung)
item.description:
Organisation: Kulturstiftung des Bundes (German Federal Cultural Foundation)

Location: Activity must be visible to audiences in Germany. Institutions headquartered in Germany or abroad may apply.

Award: No fixed ceiling, but total project costs must exceed EUR 50,000 to be eligible. The Foundation allocates up to EUR 10 million per year across this line. At least 20 percent of total project costs must be secured from own capital and/or third-party funding. No application fee.

Duration: Project-length. Projects may not begin before the jury meeting.

Deadline: Closed 31 Jul 2026

Germany's flagship open, non-thematic federal project line, and one of the largest European funders that will back a festival, exhibition programme or multi-partner convening run by an organisation rather than an individual artist. It funds large innovative projects across all artistic fields, explicitly including New Media alongside visual and performing arts, music, film, photography and architecture. There is no published maximum, but the EUR 50,000 minimum total project cost sets the scale, and at least 20 percent co-financing is mandatory. Deadlines are twice yearly at 12:00 CET: 31 July 2026 and 31 January 2027. TIMING RULE: decisions are made by an external jury meeting in May and November, and no project may start before its jury date, so plan four to six months of lead time. Non-German organisations are genuinely eligible, which is unusual at this scale, provided the project is visible in Germany and has an international dimension. Two practical barriers: the application form must be completed in German, and project communications must include a German-language version.

item.title: Arts Council of Northern Ireland: Artists' International Development Fund for Organisations (2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Northern Ireland

Location: Applicant organisations must be based in Northern Ireland; the funded activity takes place internationally, with an overseas partner or host.

Award: GBP 1,000 to 7,000. Covers art materials, residency costs, travel (mileage at 25.7p per mile plus airfare), artistic and technical fees for production or post-production, venue hire, project equipment capped at 50 percent of the request value, and IT equipment up to GBP 1,200 for laptops or GBP 500 for tablets. No application fee.

Duration: Short, early-stage international development activity.

Deadline: Closed 30 Jul 2026

The Artists' International Development Fund (Organisations) is Arts Council of Northern Ireland's route for NI-based arts organisations to take a first substantive step into international working. It is the organisations counterpart to the individual-artist AIDF under the Support for the Individual Artist Programme, which is a separate scheme with its own amount band. Grants run GBP 1,000 to 7,000 and cover art materials, residency costs, travel including airfare and mileage, artistic and technical fees for production or post-production, venue hire, and equipment capped at 50 percent of the request value. The deadline is Thursday 30 July 2026 at 12:00 noon, and the online system closes precisely at noon. Applicants must be NI-based, must have received recognition for their work there, and must not already have extensive international experience. The application must evidence genuine interest from an overseas partner or host, so a confirmed international invitation, residency offer or presentation opportunity is effectively a precondition.

item.title: Arts Council of Wales: Festivals (2026 rounds)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Wales

Location: Festival must take place in Wales and demonstrate cultural value to the local community. Welsh language integration expected.

Award: GBP 500 to 100,000 across four tiers: Small up to GBP 10,000; Large up to GBP 35,000 (1+ year track record); Large up to GBP 60,000 (3+ years, regional significance, 2+ day programme); Large up to GBP 100,000 (5+ years, national significance). Co-financing mandatory: the Council funds a maximum of 75 percent of eligible costs, so at least 25 percent of project income must come from non-Arts Council and non-Lottery sources, of which no more than 10 percent may be in-kind. No application fee.

Duration: One or two years of festival activity; two-year applications require a track record and development plan.

Deadline: Closed 29 Jul 2026

Festivals is one of the new National Lottery programmes Arts Council of Wales launched on 13 April 2026, and it is the clearest organisation-facing route for funding a public festival in Wales. It supports focused, time-limited festivals delivering high-quality arts programmes to broad audiences, in a single artform or mixed artforms, with preference given to festivals that commission, create and present new artistic work. Grants run GBP 500 to 100,000 across four tiers, with the tier ceiling tied to how long the festival has been established. Match funding is mandatory: the Council covers at most 75 percent of eligible costs and in-kind support is capped at 10 percent. There are two deadlines in 2026, both at 1pm: Wednesday 29 July 2026 and Wednesday 16 December 2026. TIMING RULE: a minimum of twelve working weeks must fall between the deadline and the project start date, so activity applied for in the July round cannot begin before roughly late October 2026. Retrospective costs are ineligible. Individual artists cannot apply.

item.title: Arts Council of Wales: Create and Engage (2026 rounds)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Wales

Location: Projects must take place mainly in Wales. Individual applicants must be Wales-based; organisations outside the UK may take part as partners provided a UK-based eligible organisation leads.

Award: Small awards up to GBP 10,000; Large awards GBP 10,001 to 60,000; exceptionally up to GBP 100,000 with prior approval from an Arts Council manager. At least 10 percent of project costs must come from non-Arts Council and non-Lottery sources. No application fee.

Duration: Project-length; activity must not already be underway at the point of application.

Deadline: Closed 29 Jul 2026

Create and Engage is Arts Council of Wales's general-purpose National Lottery programme for making and presenting arts work, launched alongside Festivals in April 2026, and is the natural fit for exhibitions, public programmes, touring and participatory events that are not structured as a festival. It funds creation, presentation, programming, touring, community participation and, for organisations only, professional development. Small awards go up to GBP 10,000 and large awards run GBP 10,001 to 60,000, with up to GBP 100,000 possible in exceptional cases with advance manager approval. At least 10 percent of project costs must come from non-Council, non-Lottery sources, a notably lighter co-financing burden than the Festivals fund's 25 percent. TIMING RULES: Small Create and Engage is rolling with no set deadlines but requires a minimum of 10 working weeks between submission and project start; Large Create and Engage has fixed 1pm deadlines on 29 July 2026, 30 September 2026 and 16 December 2026, with a minimum of 12 working weeks between deadline and project start. Non-UK organisations can participate as partners but cannot lead. Applicants cannot have an application in to more than one Arts Council fund at the same time.

item.title: The Hodder Fellowship 2027-2028 (Princeton University)
item.description:
Organisation: Princeton University, Lewis Center for the Arts

Location: Princeton, New Jersey, USA; academic-year appointment as a Visiting Fellow (no U.S. citizenship required)

Award: USD 93,000 stipend for the 10-month appointment as a Visiting Fellow. No formal teaching is involved. No application fee.

Duration: One academic year (10-month appointment), 2027-2028

Deadline: 08 Sep 2026

The Hodder Fellowship is given to artists and writers of exceptional promise to pursue independent projects at Princeton University during the academic year. Potential Hodder Fellows are composers, choreographers, performance artists, visual artists, writers, translators, or other kinds of artists or humanists who have 'much more than ordinary intellectual and literary gifts'; they are selected more 'for promise than for performance.' Given the strength of the applicant pool, most successful Fellows have published a first book or have similar achievements in their own fields; the Hodder is designed to provide Fellows with the 'studious leisure' to undertake significant new work. Fellows spend an academic year at Princeton with no formal teaching, supported by a USD 93,000 stipend for the 10-month Visiting Fellow appointment. IMPORTANT: for this cycle, applications are accepted only for the Program in Dance, the Program in Theater and Music Theater, the Program in Visual Arts, and the Department of Music. Fellowships are not intended to fund work leading to an advanced degree; one need not be a U.S. citizen to apply; previous recipients of the Princeton Arts Fellowship are not eligible. To apply, submit a resume, a 500-word project proposal, and samples of your work (writing sample, images, video links to performances, etc.). Applicants may apply for the Hodder Fellowship only twice in a lifetime. Applications are submitted via Interfolio. The application cycle closes 8 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

item.title: KHN Center for the Arts: Artist Residency
item.description:
Organisation: Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts

Location: Nebraska City, Nebraska, United States. Open internationally.

Award: USD 175/week stipend, plus free living and studio space. $35 application fee, collected via the SlideRoom application portal.

Duration: Residencies of 2-8 weeks; applications reviewed in two annual cycles (1 March and 1 September). The 2027 1st Session covers awards scheduled 4 January to 25 June 2027.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts (KHN) in Nebraska City supports established and emerging writers, visual artists, and composers/musicians by providing living and studio space that allows uninterrupted time for work, reflection, and creative growth. Residencies run 2 to 8 weeks and include free living and studio space plus a USD 175/week stipend. KHN awards approximately 30-38 residencies per session, of which roughly 8-12 go to visual artists working in various media. Categories: Writers & Poets, Visual Artists, Composers & Musicians, and Interdisciplinary Artists. Visual artists work in one of three studios (two approximately 425 sq ft and one 258 sq ft) outfitted with work tables, running water, and storage shelves; donated hand tools, a bandsaw, miter saw, and painting easels are available. Upon request, artists with previous printing experience may access the onsite Harry Duncan Letterpress Studio (SP15 Vandercook Proof Press, a 16x12 inch boxcar base for adhesive plates, furniture, fonts, and a small inventory of printmaking tools). Open internationally. Applications are reviewed twice a year (deadlines 1 March and 1 September); the 2027 1st Session (deadline 1 September 2026) is for awards scheduled 4 January to 25 June 2027. All applications must be submitted online via SlideRoom; mailed or emailed applications are not considered. A $35 application fee is collected through the portal.

item.description:
Organisation: Railyard Art Project (Railyard Park + Plaza)

Location: Santa Fe, New Mexico, United States (Railyard Park + Plaza, City-owned property under a Conservation Easement).

Award: USD 3,500 honorarium per project (two projects selected), plus marketing support and liability insurance. Funded by Santa Fe's Arts and Culture Commission. No application fee.

Duration: Two projects hosted between October 2026 and June 2027.

Deadline: 05 Aug 2026

The Railyard Art Project (RAP) facilitates temporary public art installations by established and emerging artists and arts collectives in Santa Fe's Railyard Park + Plaza. RAP is accepting proposals for temporary public art installations and creative projects; thanks to funding from Santa Fe's Arts and Culture Commission, two projects will be hosted between October 2026 and June 2027, each receiving a USD 3,500 honorarium plus marketing support and liability insurance. THEMES: the RAP Committee encourages collaboration across disciplines (art, science, history) and welcomes thoughtful, challenging, playful, and edifying art in the context of social and cultural expression and environmental sustainability. Proposed projects must physically withstand outdoor public display and engage the community by responding to the natural and social landscape of the park. SELECTION CRITERIA: overall artistic merit; context and familiarity with the proposed site; practical viability; and potential for community engagement and cultural/educational enrichment. Artists should select an eligible area of the park's open space and describe the project in detail; photos or renderings may be uploaded with the application (a map of Railyard Art Locations is linked from the program page). The RAP Committee, made up of community members and Park + Plaza stakeholders, selects and schedules the exhibitions; a formal in-person presentation may be requested depending on complexity. CONDITIONS: the park operates under a Conservation Easement, so installations cannot be located on planted areas, no staking of any kind is permitted (including during install/de-install), and nothing may be hung from trees. Artists lend artwork at their own risk (no protection against vandalism or weather damage, and artists are responsible for repairs). Installs and de-installs must be coordinated in advance with the RAP Committee or Railyard Park Conservancy staff, with a Committee or staff member on site throughout. Application deadline 5 August 2026.

item.title: Target Margin Theater: TMT Institute Fellowship 2026-27
item.description:
Organisation: Target Margin Theater

Location: Brooklyn, New York, United States (Sunset Park). Fellows must be available in person for intensives, monthly breakfasts, and excursions.

Award: USD 2,000 stipend, plus space, material resources, and collaborators to support each Fellow's experiments. No application fee.

Duration: 2026-27 season: three intensive sessions in Brooklyn (5-8 November 2026, 8-10 January 2027, 19-21 March 2027), monthly breakfasts October 2026 through May 2027, and an Open Studio weekend in June 2027.

Deadline: Closed 22 Jul 2026

Target Margin Theater invites applications for its next cohort of TMT Institute Fellows for the 2026/2027 season. The Institute is a cohort of artists who seek to radically disrupt and re-examine their existing practice without any goal or expected result: pure experimentation with no product-oriented end goal. Fellows pursue no project, no developmental stage, no deliverable; misfires, dead ends, and bad ideas are considered a fruitful part of the work. SUPPORT: TMT provides space, material resources, collaborators, and a USD 2,000 stipend. STRUCTURE: three short intensive sessions at Target Margin Theater in Brooklyn (5-8 November 2026, 8-10 January 2027, and 19-21 March 2027, all day with some evening hours), monthly breakfasts at Junior's in Brooklyn (20 October, 30 November, 4 January, 1 February, 8 March, 5 April, 3 May), and occasional excursions. After the second intensive, each Fellow commits to an exploration pursued outside group gatherings, supported by TMT resources. The season ends with an Open Studio weekend in June 2027 to share explorations with the community; this is not a performance and should not be an audience-attended, time-bounded show. WHO CAN APPLY: artists from any discipline within or outside theater, as well as production, technical, and administrative workers in the arts. Applicants must have an established, existing body of work and practice they are committed to changing; do not apply with a project. Recent graduates of training programs are unlikely to be appropriate candidates; no formal education level or degree is required. SELECTION: TMT staff and artistic community review applications and invite a handful of candidates to interview; all applicants are notified by October.
